cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Agent configurations hold the credentials for every system the agent reaches, in a store designed for orchestration rather than for secrets, so compromising the agent platform yields working credentials to each connected system directly - without the agent.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Retrieval indexes and conversation memory accumulate whatever the agent has read on behalf of every user, so a store built for relevance ends up holding the most sensitive material in the organisation, flattened and searchable without the source systems' access controls.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Connector credentials pasted into agent configuration are static, shared across every invocation and every user, and absent from the credential inventory entirely, so they are neither rotated nor revoked when the people who created them leave.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Memory and context written during one conversation are re-applied to later sessions belonging to other users without any check on where the content came from, so an instruction injected once becomes a standing behaviour change the agent treats as its own configuration.

threat: Sell Customer Identity and Behavioral Data Beyond the Scope of Consent
threat_description: A consumer identity platform collects far more than credentials. Every sign-in produces a device fingerprint, an address, a location inference, a timestamp and a behavioural sample, gathered under a security justification the customer accepted without expecting it to travel. The adversary in this case is frequently the operator: the same telemetry that scores a login for fraud is commercially valuable as an identity graph, and routing it to advertising and data broker partners is a product decision rather than an intrusion. Consent is the control, and it is the weakest part of the system — recorded as a single flag rather than a scope, rarely propagated to the partners the data already reached, and not enforced anywhere in the pipeline that moves it.

motives.motive: Monetize authentication telemetry and identity attributes beyond the consented purpose for advertising and data broker revenue

components.name: Consent and Preference Store
components.description: The record of what each customer agreed to — consent and preference records, their versions and scopes, and the interfaces through which withdrawal is registered and propagated.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-359: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Consent is stored as a boolean against an account rather than as a scope naming purposes, recipients and a duration, so the record cannot express the limit it exists to record and every downstream use reads it as blanket permission.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-285: Improper Authorization
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Analytics, marketing and partner-facing services read the customer profile through service accounts that are authorised against the store as a whole rather than against the purposes the customer agreed to, so consent constrains nothing at the point where data is actually accessed.

sub_components.name: Consent Scope Record and Withdrawal Propagation

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Withdrawal is recorded in the platform but not proven to have reached the partners the data was already shared with, so the organisation asserts a state of consent it has no mechanism to verify and no way to reverse.

components.name: Authentication Telemetry and Device Fingerprinting
components.description: The signals gathered during sign-in — device and browser fingerprints, network and location inference, behavioural biometrics and the persistent identifiers that tie sessions together over time.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-359: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Fingerprinting deployed for fraud detection produces an identifier that survives cookie clearance, private browsing and sign-out, so a mechanism justified as a security control functions as cross-context tracking that the customer cannot see, refuse or reset.

components.name: Partner Data Sharing Interface
components.description: The paths by which identity data leaves the platform — partner APIs, advertising and analytics integrations, bulk exports and the data-sharing agreements that are supposed to bound them.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Sharing interfaces expose the profile at the granularity the platform stores it rather than the granularity a partner's purpose requires, so an integration entitled to a segment membership receives the attributes the segment was derived from.

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-302: Authentication Bypass by Assumed-Immutable Data
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Export scope resolved from a partner-supplied audience or segment identifier, rather than from the agreement the credential represents, lets a partner widen its own extract to records the contract never covered.

sub_components.name: Partner Export Destination and Purpose Limitation

cwes.cwe_id: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
cwes.cwe_mapping_reason: Export destinations are storage locations shared with the recipient and rarely re-permissioned after the engagement ends, so the copy of the customer base handed over for one campaign stays readable to that partner indefinitely.
